Jain''' (born 1980) is an American physician who held leadership positions in the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) and the Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology (ONC).{{cite web|title=World Health Care Congress – Official Biography|url=http://www.worldcongress.com/speakerBio.cfm?speakerID=5769|publisher=World Healthcare Congress}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} From 2015 to 2020, he served as president and chief executive officer of the CareMore Health System. In July 2020, he joined the SCAN Group and Health Plan as its new president and CEO.{{Cite web |url=http://www.burrillreport.com/article-patientslikeme_collaborates_with_merck.html |title=PatientsLikeMe Collaborates with Merck - 08/17/2012 - the Burrill Report |access-date=2012-08-19 |archive-date=2015-01-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150118144833/http://www.burrillreport.com/article-patientslikeme_collaborates_with_merck.html |url-status=live }} He is also adjunct professor of medicine at the [[Stanford University School of Medicine]] and a Contributor at Forbes. == Early life and education == Born in [[New York City]] and raised in [[Alpine, New Jersey]], Jain attended high school at the Academy for the Advancement of Science and Technology (now part of the [[Bergen County Academies]]).[https://lifestylesmagazine.com/latest-news/110-million-in-medical-debt-relief-announced-by-sachin-h-jain/ $110 million in medical debt relief announced by Sachin H. Jain.] Lifestyles Magazine. Retrieved October 22, 2026. He received his undergraduate degree from [[Harvard College]], and while at Harvard he opened a homeless health clinic with [[Cambridge Health Alliance]].Sullivan, Tom (July 21, 2021). [https://www.healthevolution.com/insider/can-health-care-solve-the-homeless-problem-an-interview-with-scan-ceo-sachin-jain/ Can health care executives solve the homeless problem? An interview with SCAN CEO Sachin Jain.] Retrieved October 22, 2026. Jain received his medical degree (MD) from [[Harvard Medical School]] in 2006.Jain, Sachin (Spring/Summer 2026). [https://magazine.hms.harvard.edu/articles/reunion-reflections Reunion Reflections: With his 20th reunion approaching, Sachin Jain looks back on the experiences and values that he has carried with him from his time at HMS.]''Harvard Medicine'', a magazine of Harvard Medical School. Retrieved October 22, 2026.Jain, Sachin (Summer 2024). [https://magazine.hms.harvard.edu/articles/clinical-humility-and-limits-medical-knowledge Clinical Humility and the Limits of Medical Knowledge.] ''Harvard Medicine'', a magazine of Harvard Medical School. Retrieved October 22, 2026. He also earned a master's degree in business administration (MBA) from [[Harvard Business School]].Nohria, Nitin, Daisy A Wademan Dowling, and Matthew D. Breitfelder. "Sachin Jain: Life Story of a Recent MBA." Harvard Business School Case 410-039, August 2009. == Early work == Jain completed his residency in internal medicine at [[Brigham and Women's Hospital]] and Harvard Medical School, but had been granted a two-year leave mid-residency to pursue government service.{{cite web|title=World Healthcare Congress Speaker Biographies|url=http://www.worldcongress.com/speakerBio.cfm?speakerID=5769|access-date=2011-05-28|archive-date=2011-07-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726103430/http://www.worldcongress.com/speakerBio.cfm?speakerID=5769|url-status=live}} He is a founder of several nonprofit health care ventures including the Homeless Health Clinic at UniLu,{{cite news|last=Brownell|first=Matthew|title=Writer, Reformer, Physician-in-Training|url=http://harvardmagazine.com/2007/01/writer-reformer-physicia.html|newspaper=Harvard Magazine}} the Harvard Bone Marrow Initiative,{{cite news|last=Nemerenco|first=Daniela|title=Bone Marrow Drive Launched|url=http://www.thecrimson.com/article/2006/11/26/bone-marrow-drive-launched-the-harvard/|newspaper=The Harvard Crimson|access-date=2011-05-30|archive-date=2012-10-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121006083539/http://www.thecrimson.com/article/2006/11/26/bone-marrow-drive-launched-the-harvard/|url-status=live}} and the South Asian Healthcare Leadership Forum. He worked with DaVita-Bridge of Life to bring charity dialysis care to rural [[Rajasthan]], India{{cite journal|title=Bridge of Life DaVita Medical Missions|journal=Renal Business Today|date=8 November 2008|url=http://www.renalbusiness.com/articles/2008/11/bridge-of-life-davita-medical-missions.aspx|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120908123625/http://www.renalbusiness.com/articles/2008/11/bridge-of-life-davita-medical-missions.aspx|archivedate=8 September 2012}} and Medical Missions for Children to bring cleft lip and palate surgery to the region through partnership with the International Human Benefit Services Trust. While in residency, he was a researcher for Harvard Business School's Institute for Strategy and Competitiveness and worked with professors [[Michael Porter]] and [[Jim Yong Kim]] to build the emerging field of health care delivery science. He served as an expert consultant to the World Health Organization.{{cite web|title=Report on the expert consultation on positive synergies between health systems and Global Health Initiatives|url=https://www.who.int/healthsystems/hs_%26_ghi.pdf|publisher=[[World Health Organization (WHO)]]|access-date=2020-10-05|archive-date=2021-02-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210223134218/http://www.who.int/healthsystems/hs_%26_ghi.pdf|url-status=live}} He later partnered with the University of Pennsylvania's [[Amol Navathe]] and the publisher Elsevier to launch the field's charter journal, Healthcare: the Journal of Delivery Science and Innovation.{{cite web|title=Redefining Health Care Curriculum|url=http://www.hbs.edu/rhc/health_care_delivery_curriculum.html|access-date=2011-05-30|archive-date=2011-06-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110607094250/http://www.hbs.edu/rhc/health_care_delivery_curriculum.html|url-status=live}}{{cite web|title=Young President's Organization Health Care Speaker Series|url=http://www.ypohealthcare.com/BIOS/2011-WASHINGTON/Sachin%20Jain02.pdf|access-date=2011-05-30|archive-date=2012-03-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120324191156/http://www.ypohealthcare.com/BIOS/2011-WASHINGTON/Sachin%20Jain02.pdf|url-status=live}} He also collaborated with Brigham and Women's Hospital and Harvard Business School to create the John McArthur Program for Medicine Leadership.{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.hjdsi.2015.10.009 |pmid=27637817 |title=The residency-MBA program: A novel approach to training physician leaders |journal=Healthcare |volume=4 |issue=3 |pages=142–144 |year=2016 |last1=Jain |first1=Sachin H. |last2=Goodman |first2=Elaine B. |last3=Powers |first3=Brian W. |last4=Katz |first4=Joel T. }} == Career == In 2009, Jain joined the [[Office of the National Coordinator for Health Information Technology]] (ONC){{cite web|title=Official HHS Bio from Office of National Coordinator for Health Information Technology|url=http://healthit.hhs.gov/portal/server.pt/community/sachin_h._jain,_md,_mba/1819/home/17831|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120709031227/http://healthit.hhs.gov/portal/server.pt/community/sachin_h._jain,_md,_mba/1819/home/17831|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 9, 2012}} as special assistant to [[David Blumenthal]]. Jain worked with Blumenthal to implement the HITECH Provisions of the [[Recovery Act]]. He also worked on increasing electronic health record usability and {{cite web|last=Morrisey|first=John|title=Uncle Sam Wants Usability!|url=http://www.govhealthit.com/news/uncle-sam-wants-usability|publisher=Government HealthIT|access-date=2011-05-28|archive-date=2011-05-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110530175755/http://www.govhealthit.com/news/uncle-sam-wants-usability|url-status=live}} private sector engagement on behalf of ONC.{{cite journal|last=Jain|first=Sachin |author2=Seidman, Josh |author3=Blumenthal, David |title=How health plans, health systems, and others in the private sector can stimulate 'meaningful use'|journal=Health Affairs|date=September 2010|pages=1667–1670|pmid=20820024|volume=29|issue=9|doi=10.1377/hlthaff.2010.0766|doi-access=free}} Jain was recruited by his college mentor [[Donald Berwick]] as a senior advisor to the administrator at the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services and was asked to help lead the launch of the [[Center for Medicare and Medicaid Innovation]] (CMMI) that was chartered by Section 3021 of the [[Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act]]. He served briefly as its deputy director for policy and programs under Richard Gilfillan, the center's first director.{{cite journal|last=McKethan|first=Aaron|title=An Early Status Report on the Beacon Communities Program|journal=Health Affairs|url=http://content.healthaffairs.org/content/30/4/782.short|pmid=21471501|doi=10.1377/hlthaff.2011.0166|year=2011|volume=30|issue=4|pages=782–8|display-authors=etal|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}} Jain advocated within the administrator's office for speedier translation of health care delivery research into practice; an enhanced diabetes prevention benefit; and an expanded use of clinical registries.{{cite journal |last=Berwick |first=DM |author2=Jain, SH |author3=Porter, ME |title=Clinical Registries: The Opportunity for the Nation |journal=Health Affairs |year=2011 |doi=10.1377/forefront.20110511.010833 |url=https://www.healthaffairs.org/do/10.1377/forefront.20110511.010833 |access-date=2022-03-29 |archive-date=2022-03-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220329211411/https://www.healthaffairs.org/do/10.1377/forefront.20110511.010833 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }} In 2012, Jain was appointed global Chief Medical Information and Innovation Officer of Merck. At Merck, Jain built and led the company's digital health and big data group. In 2015, Jain joined [[CareMore]], an integrated health plan and delivery system. Jain left CareMore and joined SCAN Group and Health Plan, a $3.4b independent managed care company, as its president and CEO. '''SCAN Group and Health Plan''' In June 2020, Sachin Jain joined [https://www.thescangroup.org SCAN Group] and [https://www.scanhealthplan.com Health Plan], originally known as the Senior Care Action Network. Upon his appointment, Jain announced a strategic focus on growth, diversification, innovation, and improving care for diverse and underserved populations. '''CMS Lawsuit''' In 2024, Sachin Jain initiated a lawsuit against the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) in response to modifications made to the Medicare Advantage Star Ratings program. The legal action resulted in a [https://www.statnews.com/2024/06/04/medicare-advantage-scan-health-star-rating-incorrect-judge-rules/ favorable ruling] for SCAN Health Plan, yielding approximately $250 million in additional revenue. These funds were subsequently used to enhance clinical benefits for SCAN members. The case had broader implications across the Medicare Advantage landscape, prompting CMS to [https://www.wsj.com/health/healthcare/medicare-will-recalculate-quality-ratings-of-medicare-advantage-plans-eebee409?st=mqu3l57ahyaj0nb&reflink=article_copyURL_share recalculate] $1.4 billion in payments affecting 60 health plans and approximately one million beneficiaries. The outcome of the lawsuit also encouraged other insurers to pursue similar legal challenges, some of which have since been successful. == Writings == Jain has authored more than 100 publications on health care delivery innovation and health care reform. His article, "Practicing Medicine in the Age of Facebook," in the ''[[New England Journal of Medicine]]'' explores the interface between social media and the practice of clinical medicine.{{cite journal|last=Jain|first=SH|title=Practicing Medicine in the Age of Facebook|journal=New England Journal of Medicine|date=13 August 2009|volume=361|issue=7|pmid=19675328|doi=10.1056/NEJMp0901277|pages=649–51}} Two of his articles in ''[[Journal of the American Medical Association]]'', "Societal Perspectives on Physicians: Knights, Knaves, and Pawns?"{{cite journal |doi=10.1001/jama.2010.1250 |pmid=20810381 |title=Societal Perceptions of Physicians |journal=JAMA |volume=304 |issue=9 |pages=1009–10 |year=2010 |last1=Jain |first1=Sachin H. |last2=Cassel |first2=Christine K. }} (with [[Christine K. Cassel]]) and "Are Patients Knights, Knaves, and Pawn?"{{cite journal |doi=10.1001/jama.2011.694 |pmid=21610245 |title=Are Patients Knights, Knaves, or Pawns? |journal=JAMA |volume=305 |issue=20 |pages=2112–3 |year=2011 |last1=Jain |first1=Sachin H. |last2=Rother |first2=J. }} (with John Rother) build on the social theories of Julien LeGrand and apply them to physician and patient motivations. The book he co-edited with Susan Pories and Gordon Harper, "The Soul of a Doctor" has received mixed reviews.{{cite journal |doi=10.1001/jama.296.9.1141 |title=Training |journal=JAMA |volume=296 |issue=9 |pages=1141 |year=2006 |last1=Hull |first1=Sharon K. }} His article, "The Racist Patient," was mentioned in the New York Times and generated controversy about the obligation of physicians to patients with racist attitudes towards them and critical comments directed at Jain's perspective.{{cite news | url=http://well.blogs.nytimes.com/2013/07/25/when-the-patient-is-racist/ | work=The New York Times | first1=Pauline W. | last1=Chen | title=When the Patient Is Racist | date=25 July 2013 | access-date=30 July 2013 | archive-date=13 September 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130913160408/http://well.blogs.nytimes.com/2013/07/25/when-the-patient-is-racist/ | url-status=live }} == Honors == Jain is the subject of a Harvard Business School case study written by dean [[Nitin Nohria]].{{cite web|last=Nohria|first=Nitin|title=Sachin Jain: Life Story of A Recent MBA|url=http://hbr.org/product/sachin-jain-life-story-of-a-recent-mba/an/410039-PDF-ENG|publisher=Harvard Business School Press}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Jain was selected to Boston Business Journal's 40 under 40 list.{{cite news | url=http://www.bizjournals.com/boston/blog/bottom_line/2012/09/bbj-40-under-40-2012.html | title=BBJ names 2012's 40 under 40 honorees | access-date=2013-09-17 | archive-date=2013-09-17 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130917074647/http://www.bizjournals.com/boston/blog/bottom_line/2012/09/bbj-40-under-40-2012.html | url-status=live }} He has been named several times to Modern Healthcare's lists of most influential minority health leaders, most influential clinical executives, and most influential leaders in healthcare. In 2024, he was named one of American healthcare's most influential people in healthcare. In 2025 he was named to the [https://www.beckershospitalreview.com/lists/great-leaders-in-healthcare-2025/ Becker’s Hospital Review] list of great leaders and the Los Angeles Business Journal added him to its annual [https://labusinessjournal.com/la500-2025/health-care-2025/la500-2025-sachin-jain/ LA 500 list]. == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == * {{Official website|http://healthit.hhs.gov/portal/server.pt/community/sachin_h._jain,_md,_mba/1819/home/17831}} *[http://harvardmagazine.com/2007/01/writer-reformer-physicia.html Profile of Sachin Jain from Harvard Magazine] *[http://hms.harvard.edu/deans_report/pdfs/HMS_DR_0708.pdf Profile from Harvard Medical School Annual Report] *[http://www.alumni.hbs.edu/bulletin/2007/june/profiles.html Harvard Business School Class of 2007 Profiles] *[http://www.worldcongress.com/speakerBio.cfm?speakerID=5769 Bio from World Healthcare Congress]{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Jain, Sachin H.}} [[Category:1980 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American academics of Indian descent]] [[Category:American chief executives in the health care industry]] [[Category:American medical doctors]] [[Category:American medical doctors of Indian descent]] [[Category:American Jains]] [[Category:Bergen County Academies alumni]] [[Category:Harvard Business School alumni]] [[Category:Harvard Medical School alumni]] [[Category:Harvard College alumni]] [[Category:Indian scholars]] [[Category:Paul & Daisy Soros Fellows]]
